entries.text: When output at one mine falls and other mines do not add the same amount, world mine output is lower than it would otherwise have been.
When a stopped mine is expected to restart in stages, how long the lost output lasts depends on when each stage restarts.
When ore grades at operating mines fall, each tonne of ore holds less copper, so output falls unless more ore is mined and processed.
When a producer approves an expansion, the added output enters future mine supply only if it is built as planned, and a projection includes it only if its method counts approved projects.
